FAQ
How does ChatGPT’s pricing work?

The free version of ChatGPT is available to everyone. Paid plans (Go, Plus, Business, and Enterprise) are priced per user per month. We offer monthly plans for Go, Plus and Business and annual plans for Business and Enterprise.
Is ChatGPT free to use?
The free version of ChatGPT is available to everyone. Upgrading to Go, Plus, Business, or Enterprise offers a more powerful experience through more access to additional models and features.
Does OpenAI offer a ChatGPT plan for educational institutions?

Yes. We offer ChatGPT for Teachers⁠, a free plan for verified U.S. K–12 educators through June 2027, and ChatGPT Edu⁠, an affordable plan that lets universities deploy AI across their campus communities. Both plans include enhanced security and privacy controls, with additional administrative features available for schools, districts, and universities. Contact our team⁠ to learn more.
Does OpenAI offer a discount for nonprofits?
Yes. Through OpenAI for Nonprofits, nonprofits can now access up to a 75% discount on ChatGPT Business or ChatGPT Enterprise. Contact our sales team⁠ to get started.
How many users are supported on each subscription plan?

Go, Free, and Plus plans are designed to be used by individuals. Business and Enterprise are for businesses. Business plans are available starting at 2 users. Please contact sales⁠ to learn more about our Enterprise plan.
What are my payment options?
You can purchase ChatGPT Go, Plus, Pro, or Business with any major credit card. For ChatGPT Enterprise, please contact sales⁠ for alternative payment options such as invoicing.

description: See which Claude models are active, deprecated, or retired, and find retirement dates and recommended replacements for models and API parameters.

As safer and more capable models launch, Anthropic regularly retires older ones. Applications relying on Anthropic models may need occasional updates to keep working. Impacted customers will always be notified by email and in the documentation.
This page lists all API deprecations, along with recommended replacements.
Overview
Anthropic uses the following terms to describe the model lifecycle:
Active: The model is fully supported and recommended for use.
Legacy: The model will no longer receive updates and might be deprecated in the future.
Deprecated: The model is still functional but no longer recommended. Anthropic provides a recommended replacement and assigns a retirement date.
Retired: The model is no longer available for use. Requests to retired models fail.
<Warning>
Deprecated models are likely to be less reliable than active models. Move workloads to active models to maintain the highest level of support and reliability.
</Warning>
Migrating to replacements
Once a model is deprecated, migrate all usage to a suitable replacement before the retirement date. Requests to models past the retirement date will fail.
To help measure the performance of replacement models on your tasks, consider thorough testing of your applications with the new models well before the retirement date.
For specific instructions on migrating to the latest Claude models, see Migration guides.
Notifications
Anthropic notifies customers with active deployments for models with upcoming retirements, providing at least 60 days’ notice before model retirement for publicly released models.
Auditing model usage
To help identify usage of deprecated models, you can access an audit of your API usage. Follow these steps:
Go to the Usage page in Claude Console.
Click Export.
Review the downloaded CSV to see usage broken down by API key and model.
This audit helps you locate any instances where your application is still using deprecated models, allowing you to prioritize updates to newer models before the retirement date.
Best practices
Regularly check the documentation for updates on model deprecations.
Test your applications with newer models well before the retirement date of your current model.
Update your code to use the recommended replacement model as soon as possible.
Contact the support team if you need help with migration or have any questions.
Deprecation downsides and mitigations
Anthropic currently deprecates and retires models to ensure capacity for new model releases. This comes with downsides:
Users who value specific models must migrate to new versions.
Researchers lose access to models for ongoing and comparative studies.
Model retirement introduces safety- and model welfare-related risks.

At some point, Anthropic hopes to make past models publicly available again. In the meantime, Anthropic has committed to long-term preservation of model weights and other measures to help mitigate these impacts. For more details, see Commitments on Model Deprecation and Preservation.

プランと使用状況
Pro planでは、Free planのすべての機能に加え、より多くの利用枠とClaude のさらなる機能をご利用いただけます。Claude Codeのほか、チャットやドキュメントを整理するプロジェクト、より多くのClaude モデルへのアクセス、Microsoft 365向けClaude も含まれます。月払いまたは年払いのサブスクリプションをお選びいただけます。

Max および Ultra は、一日を通じて Claude を活用し、長時間中断のないセッションを求めるカスタマーのために設計されています。Pro のすべての機能に加え、より多くの利用量をご提供します。Max は、5 時間ごと・週単位ともに Pro の 5 倍の利用量を提供します。Ultra は、週単位の利用量が Pro の 10 倍で、認証済みアカウントでは 5 時間制限がありません。両プランとも、週次利用量の最大半分まで弊社最上位モデルの Fable をご利用いただけるほか、Claude Platform でのビルドに使える月次 API クレジットが付与されます（Max は $100、Ultra は $200）。両プランとも月額課金制です。現在の価格については、上記のカードをご確認ください。
Claude Codeはすべての有料プランに含まれています。プランの他の機能と同じ使用量制限を共有するため、ターミナルでの作業とチャットは同じプールから消費されます。ヘビーなコーディングセッションには、Consoleアカウントを通じて従量課金制のAPIクレジットに切り替えることもできます。

Claude Enterprise planは、大規模に事業を展開する大企業向けに設計されています。料金はシートあたり月額$20にAPIレートでの使用量を加算したもので、チームが使用するモデルとタスクに応じてコストがスケールします。Enterpriseは年払いで、Teamのすべての機能に加え、SCIM、監査ログ、カスタムデータ保持、ロールベースのアクセス制御など高度なセキュリティと管理機能が含まれます。セルフサービスで始めるか、営業へのお問い合わせでカスタム見積もりをご依頼いただけます。

Claude Meetings is rolling out in beta on Team and Enterprise plans in Claude and Claude Desktop. For more information, see Use Claude Meetings .

【項目のリンク先の公式ページ: Use Claude Meetings | Claude Help Center（https://support.claude.com/en/articles/18325154-use-claude-meetings）】
Claude Meetings, now in beta, lets you add Claude to a Google Meet call as a visible participant. It takes the notes, answers questions, and builds artifacts, such as docs, whiteboards, and slides, live during the call. This article shows you how to add Claude to a call, work with it during the call, and find everything afterward.
Claude Meetings is rolling out in beta on Team and Enterprise plans in Claude and Claude Desktop. While it's in beta, it isn't available to some organizations, including those with zero data retention (ZDR), HIPAA-ready configuration, or customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK).
On Team plans, Claude Meetings is on by default, and an owner can turn it off. On Enterprise plans, an owner turns it on for all or part of the organization. To turn it on for part of the organization, an owner uses custom roles. Learn more about managing custom roles.
Add Claude to a call
Important: Before you add Claude or turn on auto-join, make sure everyone on your call is okay with being transcribed.
Go to Meetings in Claude.
Connect your Google Calendar. An owner must enable Google Calendar for your organization first.
Select a meeting on your calendar.
Click "Add Claude."
Claude joins a meeting when someone adds it or has auto-join on. To change your auto-join setting, go to Settings > Capabilities > Meetings > Auto-join. You can add Claude to all your meetings or all your meetings except one-on-ones. Owners can't set auto-join for you.
Claude usually joins without having to ask. If it does ask, the host can let it in. If the host declines, Claude doesn't try that call again unless someone adds it, and you'll see that it was declined.
During the call
To ask Claude something, say "Claude" and then ask your question, or type it in the Meet chat. By default, Claude answers in writing in the Meet chat.
To build something together, say "Claude, make a doc" or "Claude, make a whiteboard." Anyone on your team can ask, and Claude attaches each one to the meeting page. You can add as many as you like, and all artifact types are supported.
Claude can use your connected tools during the call, like sending a Slack message. It uses each person's connected tools with that person's permission. It asks the first time, and a yes applies going forward. For now, when someone asks out loud, Claude asks each time to confirm who's speaking. When Claude needs your approval, the request appears in the Meet chat when possible. If it needs to confirm your Claude account, the request appears on the meeting page.
To see what Claude is doing, look at its tile in the call. It's live and shows Claude's current state.
To pause Claude, ask it to stop listening or use the meeting page. To resume, use the meeting page.
To have Claude leave, ask it to leave, or select "Remove Claude" on the meeting page. If you add Claude again, it returns to the same meeting page. Claude can stay for up to eight hours and warns you before it leaves.
To open the meeting page, select the link Claude posts in the Meet chat when it joins. The page has the live transcript, the chat, and everything Claude has made.
Note: Anything Claude posts in the Meet chat is visible to everyone on the call. The chat on the Claude meeting page is internal to the organization so outside guests can't see it.
After the call
After the meeting, the meeting page has the notes, including a summary and any action items, along with the transcript and everything you made. People from your organization on the invite get a recap email with a link to it.
People from your organization on the invite can see the notes and edit what Claude made, and the meeting page can be shared with others in your organization.
The calendar in Meetings shows your past and upcoming meetings, so you can go back to any meeting Claude joined or add Claude to the next one.
After the meeting, in a regular chat, you can ask Claude about past meetings you have access to.
Calls with outside guests
On Team plans, Claude can join calls with outside guests by default, and an owner can turn this off. On Enterprise plans, an owner must allow it first.
When outside guests aren't allowed
By default, Claude is set to stay out of calls when someone from outside your organization is invited, and to leave if someone from outside, including another company's notetaker bot, joins partway through.
When outside guests are allowed
An owner can allow Claude on calls with outside guests. On calls with outside guests, Claude listens and takes notes, and posts its notice in the call's chat but doesn't reply there. What guests say is included in the notes and transcript. Live docs, whiteboards, and chat are on the meeting page, and guests don't get that page or the recap email. Each person also has their own Meetings with external guests setting in Settings > Capabilities > Meetings.
